name: Orvaine Hailbreak Shell
description: A no-nonsense rain shell from Orvaine's utility line, cut slightly longer in the back to cover the waistband when leaning forward — a detail that sounds minor until you've spent a shift in the rain. The Hailbreak is made from a three-layer bonded nylon ripstop with a durable water-repellent finish that beads and sheds even in sustained downpour. The cut is relaxed enough to layer over a hoodie without binding. Packable into its own chest pocket, compressing down to roughly the size of a folded paperback. Comes in four colors: slate grey, deep navy, safety olive, and a high-visibility amber-yellow version used by corridor maintenance crews. Pit zips for ventilation. Fully seam-taped.
what_it_says: Practical, unsentimental, and well-chosen. You understand weather and you dress for it. The Hailbreak is the jacket of people who spend real time outside — not commuting through climate-controlled tubes, but actually out in it.
worn_by: anyone who works outdoors in the corridor's unpredictable lake-effect weather
story_hooks: The high-vis amber version is standard issue for corridor maintenance, which means wearing one is a low-effort way to move through restricted infrastructure zones without immediate challenge.

Orvaine quietly discontinued the Hailbreak's original formula two years ago — current production uses a cheaper bonded layer that delaminates after heavy use. Vintage stock from before the reformulation trades at a premium on secondary markets.
A witness to something they shouldn't have seen was wearing a Hailbreak in slate grey. There are forty thousand of them in active circulation in the city.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian rain shell with a slightly extended back hem, creating an asymmetrical silhouette when worn. Clean, minimalist lines with no excess ornamentation. Reads as practical workwear rather than fashion—the kind of jacket that disappears into background functionality until you need it.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and oversized through the torso, designed to layer over hoodies and thermal wear without restriction. Sleeves are straight and untatpered. The extended back hem sits 2-3 inches lower than standard jackets, covering the waistband when leaning or bending.
physical_description.primary_material: Three-layer bonded nylon ripstop with durable water-repellent (DWR) finish. Synthetic, engineered for maximum weather resistance with minimal weight.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, slightly glossy nylon exterior. Ripstop weave creates a subtle grid pattern visible on close inspection. Seams are visibly taped, appearing as flat, reinforced lines running along shoulders and sides.
physical_description.color_scheme: Slate grey (neutral Tier 3 standard), deep navy, safety olive, and high-visibility amber-yellow. No patterns or graphics—solid utilitarian colorways.
physical_description.closures: Full front zipper with storm flap. Pit zip vents on both sides for thermal regulation. Friction-fit elastic cuffs at wrists. No visible buttons or snaps.
distinctive_features: Extended back hem—cuts 2-3 inches lower to cover waistband during forward-leaning work
Pit zips for ventilation in rain and exertion
Fully taped seams throughout for weatherproofing
Integrated chest pocket serves as compression sack—entire jacket packs into itself
Minimal branding—small woven Orvaine label only
No hood (designed for layering under separate headwear)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional workwear. Affordable, durable, and ubiquitous among working-class and maintenance crews throughout the GLMZ.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by corridor maintenance workers, delivery personnel, field technicians, and anyone spending extended hours exposed to GLMZ weather systems. Signals practical priorities over status. The amber-yellow variant is standard issue for municipal infrastructure crews.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and weathered. Beading effect on DWR coating diminishes slightly with repeated washing, but water-shedding remains effective for years. Visible creases from packdown. Minimal visible wear—nylon ripstop resists tears and discoloration.
